weeks.rationale: Race week — the event is Sunday 2 Aug. Monday through Wednesday still train normally: one true threshold session six days out (far enough to supercompensate rather than cost freshness), paired with a two-set heavy-lower touch, then a short three-round station primer on Wednesday. The final three days freshen — easy plus openers Thursday, full rest Friday, a 25-minute primer Saturday. Volume lands at the low end of the band (~43.5 km including the 8 km raced) because the freshen cuts volume, not intensity.
weeks.methodology: A freshen cuts volume while holding intensity, which sheds fatigue without shedding fitness — the athlete's chosen half-week abbreviation of the classic taper, justified by the short race and an err-high bias. Monday's threshold work is anchored on the measured LT2 rather than the sub-threshold race pace used previously, keeping the session out of the grey zone where the stimulus is neither easy nor productive. Heavy strength is reduced to two top sets rather than dropped: taper evidence supports cutting volume and keeping intensity, so a low-volume, high-intensity lift preserves neural drive at negligible fatigue cost. Plyometrics are omitted entirely this week since residual leg stiffness is the one thing that cannot be recovered by Sunday. Easy days stay genuinely easy, well below the Z2 ceiling, so the two quality touches land on fresh legs.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x6' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: RUN: 15 min easy warmup -> 4x6 min at threshold (155-163 bpm, 4:48-4:34/km) with 2 min jog recovery -> 10 min easy cooldown. GYM (separate session, same day): back squat 2x3 @ 100 kg RPE 8, trap-bar deadlift 2x3 @ 130 kg RPE 8, 3 min full rest, concentric as fast as possible. Two top sets only — stop there.

steps.target: RPE 8 (~2 RIR), 3 min rest, explosive concentric
RPE 8, 3 min rest, no grinding reps

sessions.purpose: Last real quality of the block: hold LT2 and neural drive six days out.
sessions.why: Threshold is the shared ceiling for the 21k and the race's running, and six days is enough for the stimulus to settle rather than linger — but only 24 min of work, not a full peak dose, because nothing gained this week outweighs arriving fresh. The lift is two top sets rather than a session: taper logic keeps intensity and cuts volume, and heavy low-rep work at this dose costs almost no recovery while preserving the power the race demands.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min genuinely easy, HR <=138 bpm, no faster than 5:22/km, conversational throughout. If the legs are heavy from Monday, go slower — do not shorten.
sessions.purpose: Carry easy volume and clear Monday's fatigue.
sessions.why: Polarized training depends on the easy days being truly easy; this is the day that pays for Monday and sets up Wednesday's primer. No strides or pickups — any grey-zone effort here would blunt both quality touches of the week.

sessions.title: Short Station Primer (3 rounds)
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy warmup + drills -> 3 rounds of 1000 m at ~4:50-4:55/km straight into one station: R1 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R2 sled pull 153 kg / 50 m; R3 wall balls 9 kg x 40 to 3.0 m. Rehearse the transitions deliberately — controlled, never maximal. 5 min jog cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Final rehearsal of running on pre-fatigued legs and of station transitions.
sessions.why: Compromised running is the demand no pure run session trains, and three rounds keeps that pattern live in the legs; it is capped at three because this is the last station work before Sunday and the freshen starts tomorrow. Loads stay at competition standard for specificity, but the volume is a third of a full sim.

sessions.title: Easy + Openers
sessions.prescription: 30 min easy (HR <=138 bpm) + 4x20 s relaxed strides at race pace with full walk-back recovery. Freshen begins: short and snappy, nothing draining.
sessions.purpose: Keep neuromuscular sharpness while volume drops.
sessions.why: Strides maintain turnover at essentially zero fatigue cost, which is exactly what a freshen wants: intensity retained, volume cut. Three days out there is no fitness left to gain, so the run is short and the strides are the only quality.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Mobility, hydration, and sleep. The usual Sunday rest day moves here because Sunday is race day.
sessions.purpose: Bank recovery two days out.
sessions.why: A full rest day 48 h out lets the last of the week's fatigue clear while the freshen is still short enough to avoid feeling flat. Nothing productive can be added at this point that would not cost more than it returns.

sessions.title: Pre-Race Primer
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy jog + 3x30 s at race pace (~4:50/km) with full recovery + dynamic drills. Rehearse the race-morning routine (timing, breakfast, kit). Finish feeling like you could have done much more.

steps.target: leg swings, A-skips, a few squats and lunges

sessions.purpose: Wake the legs up without touching tomorrow's freshness.
sessions.why: A short opener with a few race-pace touches keeps the nervous system primed after a rest day, which usually beats total rest the day before. Held under 25 min so it primes rather than tires.

sessions.title: RACE: Aug 2 event (Mixto)
sessions.prescription: RACE DAY. 8 km of running broken by eight stations: deadlift 100 reps @ 34 kg; wall balls 100 reps @ 6 kg; burpee broad jump 80 m; sandbag lunges 100 m @ 10 kg; thrusters 100 reps @ 29 kg; farmers carry 200 m @ 2x15 kg; tyre flip-over 80 m; obstacle course to finish. PACING: run the first two legs at ~5:00-5:05/km, deliberately slower than feels right. STATION STRATEGY: break every 100-rep set into planned chunks from rep one (thrusters 5x20, wall balls 5x20, deadlifts 4x25) with 10-15 s between chunks — do not start unbroken. Empty the tank only on the final run and the obstacle course.

steps.target: 4x25, short breaks, keep the back flat
chest tall, knee light to the floor
5x20 — the biggest blow-up risk of the day
one drop maximum, grip before legs

sessions.purpose: Race the event and bank a competitive-effort data point for the Nov 14 build.
sessions.why: This is the target the block pointed at; execution beats heroics. The stations here are high-rep and light, so the limiter is local muscular fatigue rather than the run — which is why the pacing plan is conservative early and the 100-rep sets are pre-broken from the first rep. Log the running splits under fatigue: those are the numbers that carry into the November macrocycle.

weeks.rationale: Post-race week, first week of the Nov 14 base build (15 weeks out). Per your preference we take a single easy recovery day Monday, then train through in-band the rest of the week — not a full recovery week. Emphasis shifts to aerobic volume with one moderate quality touch and a return to heavy strength; nothing peaked. If the race leaves you beaten up, ask and I'll soften Wednesday/Thursday.
weeks.methodology: Base phase prioritizes easy aerobic volume to rebuild the engine for the 21k and the next Hyrox, with sparing intensity. A single recovery day respects race stress without detraining. Heavy strength returns for running economy; it is placed to make a clean hard day rather than blunting an easy one. Long-run volume climbs back toward base.

sessions.title: Active Recovery
sessions.prescription: Very easy 20-30 min: walk, easy spin, or mobility + light stretching. No running, no load. The one recovery day after the race.
sessions.purpose: Flush race-day fatigue and soreness.
sessions.why: One low-stress day clears the worst of the race DOMS so the rest of the week can be productive; more than a day off is unnecessary at your recovery bias.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational. First run back — ease in, cut short if the legs are still heavy.
sessions.purpose: Re-establish easy aerobic rhythm.
sessions.why: Gentle re-entry to running after the race; easy volume rebuilds the base without stressing legs that just raced.

sessions.title: Tempo 3x8'
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy warmup -> 3x8 min @ tempo (147-155 bpm, 5:04-4:48/km) with 2 min jog -> 10 min easy cooldown. Tempo, not threshold — controlled first quality back.
sessions.purpose: Reintroduce sustained aerobic-threshold work at a controlled intensity.
sessions.why: Tempo rather than full threshold eases quality back in the week after a race; still enough stimulus to hold the aerobic ceiling built for Hyrox.

sessions.title: Heavy Lower + Easy Shakeout (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym): 20 min very easy shakeout, HR <=135 bpm. PM (gym): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg (RPE 8, 3 min rest); trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg; weighted step-up 3x8 @ 20 kg/hand. Judge by RIR, not HR. No plyometrics.
sessions.purpose: Restore heavy strength for running economy and sled power in the new build.
sessions.why: Heavy low-rep strength is the main economy driver; reintroduced now to anchor the 15-week Hyrox build. Paired with only a light shakeout so it is a clean strength day.

sessions.title: Easy + Strides
sessions.prescription: 50 min easy (HR <=138 bpm) + 6x20 s relaxed strides with full recovery. Easy volume with a light neuromuscular touch.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic volume plus economy pop.
sessions.why: Builds base km toward the 47-58 target; strides add turnover without grey-zone cost the day before the long run.

sessions.title: Long Run
sessions.prescription: 100 min steady easy, HR <=142 bpm, ~5:30-5:50/km throughout. Pure aerobic long run — no surges this week, just time on feet rebuilding the 21k base.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic endurance for the 21k and the Hyrox base.
sessions.why: The long run is the primary endurance driver; kept purely easy the week after a race to build volume without adding intensity stress.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or an easy walk.
sessions.purpose: Recovery.
sessions.why: The fixed weekly rest day, back in its normal Sunday slot now the race is done.

weeks.rationale: Base build, 14 weeks to Hyrox #2. A full in-band base week (~50 km) with quality reintroduced: one true threshold session (paired with heavy lower to make a clean hard day) and one base-level compromised sim to keep race skills alive. Everything else is easy aerobic volume; Sunday rest. This is engine-building, not peaking.
weeks.methodology: Base phase leans on large easy volume with sparing high-quality threshold to raise LT2 — the shared lever for the 21k and Hyrox running. Heavy strength continues for economy and is clustered onto the threshold day so easy days stay easy; plyometrics sit on an easy day. A single moderate sim maintains compromised-running skill far out from the race without the specificity load of a peak block.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 55 min easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational. Sets up the week's first quality on Tuesday.
sessions.purpose: Easy aerobic base.
sessions.why: Opens the week with genuinely easy volume so Tuesday's threshold is sharp; easy running is where the aerobic base is built.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x8' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym) THRESHOLD: 15 min easy warmup -> 4x8 min @ threshold (155-163 bpm, 4:48-4:34/km) with 2:30 jog -> 10 min easy cooldown. PM (gym): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg (RPE 8, progress if >2 RIR); trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg. No plyometrics today.
sessions.purpose: Raise LT2 and maintain strength economy in one clean hard day.
sessions.why: Threshold volume nudged up to 4x8' as base fitness rebuilds; paired with heavy lower to cluster the hard feel. Progress the squat load if it leaves >2 RIR — that is the fix for it feeling easy.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min genuinely easy, HR <=138 bpm. Recovery between the week's two hard days.
sessions.purpose: Easy recovery volume.
sessions.why: Separates Tuesday's threshold from Thursday's sim with a truly easy day, protecting both.

sessions.title: Base Compromised Sim (4 rounds)
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy warmup -> 4 rounds: 1000 m run @ race pace (~4:55/km, 150-160 bpm) into one station - R1 ski erg 1000 m; R2 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R3 farmers carry 2x32 kg / 200 m; R4 wall balls 9 kg x 50. 5 min jog cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Maintain compromised-running skill and station endurance far out from the race.
sessions.why: Four rounds keeps the race pattern alive during base without the specificity load of a peak sim; a lighter dose than the peak-week five rounds since the race is 14 weeks away.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo Primer (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym): 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm. PM (gym, ~15 min): box jumps 4x3 + hurdle hops 3x5, full recovery. Explosive snap only.
sessions.purpose: Easy volume plus explosive maintenance.
sessions.why: Plyometrics preserve power for sleds and running economy; kept on an easy day per the concurrent-interference window, and the run stays easy before Saturday's long run.

sessions.title: Long Run + Race-Pace Finish
sessions.prescription: 80 min easy (HR <=142 bpm, ~5:30-5:50/km) -> 4x3 min @ race pace (~4:55/km) with 2 min easy jog -> 6 min easy cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Build 21k endurance with a light race-pace touch.
sessions.why: Long-run volume climbs as base builds; the short race-pace finish keeps specificity without a third hard running day.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or an easy walk.
sessions.purpose: Recovery.
sessions.why: The fixed weekly rest day; protects recovery and closes the block cleanly.

weeks.rationale: Third base week of the Nov 14 macrocycle re-entry, 13 weeks out. Volume sits at the top of the band (~58 km) with the standard base shape: one threshold session, one compromised sim, a long run, and easy volume carrying the rest. Nothing is peaked here — the job is accumulating easy kilometres and holding one quality touch per system.
weeks.methodology: Base weeks are built on a large easy fraction with a small, potent dose of hard work, which is the robust finding across elite endurance training. One threshold session anchored on the measured LT2 raises the ceiling both the 21k and the race's running share. Heavy compound strength supports running economy and is paired with the hard run so the easy days stay clean, while plyometrics sit on an easy-run day because same-session concurrent training is the one place power is meaningfully blunted. Volume steps up gradually rather than spiking.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min easy, HR <=138 bpm, no faster than 5:22/km. Conversational throughout.
sessions.purpose: Open the week with unambiguous easy volume.
sessions.why: Easy kilometres are the bulk of what raises aerobic base; keeping them strictly below the Z2 ceiling is what makes tomorrow's threshold session sharp. No pickups — the grey zone buys nothing.

sessions.title: Threshold 5x6' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: RUN: 15 min easy warmup -> 5x6 min at threshold (155-163 bpm, 4:48-4:34/km) with 2 min jog recovery -> 10 min cooldown. GYM (separate session, same day): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg RPE 8; trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg RPE 8; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg. Full 2-3 min rest, explosive concentric, never to failure. Add load on any lift where the top set leaves more than 2 reps in reserve.

steps.target: RPE 7-8, 2 min rest, squeeze at lockout

sessions.purpose: Raise LT2 and load the posterior chain on one consolidated hard day.
sessions.why: Threshold is the highest-return lever for both goals, and 30 min of work is a full base-week dose without tipping into a session that needs two days to clear. The lift shares the day so the easy days stay genuinely easy; no plyometrics here because explosive work loses most in the same session as a hard run.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm. Pure recovery from Tuesday's double.
sessions.purpose: Recover between the week's two quality days.
sessions.why: The day after a hard double has to be genuinely easy or the sim on Thursday degrades; this is where the polarized distribution is won or lost.

sessions.title: Base Compromised Sim (4 rounds)
sessions.prescription: 10 min warmup -> 4 rounds of 1000 m at ~4:50-4:55/km straight into one station: R1 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R2 sled pull 153 kg / 50 m; R3 farmers carry 2x32 kg / 200 m; R4 wall balls 9 kg x 40 to 3.0 m. 5 min jog cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Train running economy under station-induced fatigue at competition loads.
sessions.why: Compromised running is the race-specific demand no pure run reproduces, and station loads stay at the Pro standard so the neuromuscular cost matches race day. Four rounds is a base-week dose — enough to keep the pattern, short of the five-round sims that belong in a peak week.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo + Heavy Upper (double)
sessions.prescription: RUN: 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm. GYM (separate session, same day): box jump 4x3 and standing broad jump 3x3, full recovery between sets, maximum intent. Then weighted pull-up 4x4 and overhead press 4x4 at RPE 8. Upper loads are still unbaselined — pick the weight that leaves 1-2 reps in reserve, log what you actually used, and report it so the numbers get fixed in config.

steps.target: full recovery, maximum intent, land soft
RPE 8 (~2 RIR) — log the load used

sessions.purpose: Explosive and upper-body strength on an easy-run day, plus easy volume.
sessions.why: Plyometrics improve running economy but lose most of their effect when stacked on a hard run, so they belong here on an easy day. Vertical pull and press carry directly to the pulling and overhead stations. Loads are RPE-anchored rather than prescribed in kg because the upper-body baseline has not been reported yet.

sessions.title: Long Run
sessions.prescription: 16 km steady, HR <=145 bpm for the first 13 km, then the last 3 km lifted to tempo (147-155 bpm, ~5:04-4:48/km). Check Pa:HR decoupling afterwards — target is under 5%.
sessions.purpose: Build aerobic durability and practise running strong on tired legs.
sessions.why: The long run is the single biggest contributor to the easy-volume base, and the tempo finish trains holding pace as fatigue accumulates without turning the day into a third hard session. Decoupling under 5% is the read on whether the base is actually deepening.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Mobility and sleep.
sessions.purpose: Absorb the week.
sessions.why: Adaptation happens on the rest day; a single full day off is what makes a 58 km week with two quality sessions repeatable rather than a spike.
